<page>
 Fort Bend County District Court
 Cause No. 2023-CV-0016
 Jennifer Tyler, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Oral Deposition of Jennifer Tyler
Date:
February 8, 2024
Location:
Offices of Santiago & Romero Law Group
Examining attorney:
Richard Marshall, Ashford & Lyle LLP
Defending attorney:
Eric Phillips, Santiago & Romero Law Group
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not put my full name in a transcript for this, but I understand the names will be handled through the protective order.
You can refer to me as the plaintiff.
Q: That's fine. Where were you on the day of the collision?
A: I was driving home from work on a two-lane road in Pasadena, Texas. It was late afternoon and traffic was moderate.
Q: Describe what happened.
A: A vehicle coming from the opposite direction drifted over the center line. I braked and steered to the right, but we still made
contact. It was a head-on impact, though not a hard one. The airbags did not deploy.
Q: How fast were you traveling?
A: The speed limit was around thirty-five. I wasn't going much faster than that, maybe slightly under.
Q: Did you feel pain immediately after the collision?
A: Not right away. I felt shaken and a little stiff. By the next morning my neck was sore and my lower back had a dull ache that
kept getting worse over the following days.
Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes. A family member drove me to an urgent care clinic that same evening, and then I saw my primary care doctor about a
week later. They referred me to a physical therapist.
Q: What treatment have you received since then?
A: I've been going to physical therapy about two or three times a week. I was also prescribed muscle relaxers and an
anti-inflammatory medication. I did a few sessions of massage therapy on my own, which my doctor said was fine as long as I
kept up the exercises at home.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Mostly it's made simple things harder. I used to coach my kid's soccer team on weekends, and I had to hand that off for a
while. Sitting at my desk for long stretches leaves my back aching, and I've had trouble sleeping on my left side. I still do most of
my own errands, but I take more breaks than I used to.
Q: Have you returned to work?
A: Yes, I went back to work after about two weeks, though I was on modified duties for a time and I stand up more often now.
</page>
